content_voiceover: Now we get to PRETEXT and POST-TEXT staging, which is the radiographic, pretreatment counterpart to the surgical Evans system, and it's the staging system actually used in most modern liver tumor protocols. Unlike Evans, PRETEXT is assigned before any treatment based on imaging alone, using those four liver sections from the previous slide, right posterior, right anterior, left medial, and left lateral. Stage one means three contiguous sections are tumor-free, so only one section is involved. Stage two means two contiguous sections are tumor-free, so two sections are involved. Stage three means only one contiguous section is tumor-free, so three sections are involved. And Stage four means no contiguous sections are tumor-free, meaning the tumor involves all four sections. POST-TEXT uses this same grading system but is reassessed after neoadjuvant chemotherapy to guide surgical planning. On top of the basic stage, any group can carry one or more annotation factors that flag additional risk, V for tumor ingrowth into the vena cava or all three hepatic veins, P for ingrowth into the portal vein or its bifurcation, E for extrahepatic contiguous tumor extension, F for multifocal tumor, R for tumor rupture at diagnosis, C for caudate lobe involvement, N for lymph node involvement, and M for distant metastasis. These annotation factors are what actually drive a lot of the poor prognosis features you saw on the hepatoblastoma summary slide.
keypoints: PRETEXT is imaging-based staging assigned before treatment; POST-TEXT reassesses after chemo
Stage I: 3 contiguous sections tumor-free (1 section involved)
Stage II: 2 sections tumor-free; Stage III: 1 section tumor-free; Stage IV: no tumor-free sections
Annotation factors: V (vena cava/hepatic veins), P (portal vein), E (extrahepatic), F (multifocal)
Additional annotations: R (rupture), C (caudate lobe), N (nodes), M (metastasis)
keypoint_voiceover: PRETEXT stages liver tumors by imaging before treatment, counting tumor-free liver sections out of four, Stage one has three tumor-free sections and Stage four has none tumor-free. POST-TEXT repeats this after chemotherapy. Annotation factors V, P, E, F, R, C, N, and M flag vena cava, portal vein, extrahepatic extension, multifocality, rupture, caudate involvement, nodal disease, and metastasis.
